template_P04_biotech.target: VP Research or Head of Drug Delivery at neuro/biotech company (AbbVie, Eli Lilly, Alector, Denali)
template_P04_biotech.subject: P-04: Pulsation-synchronized catalytic CSF clearance — engineering frozen, biology program defined
template_P04_biotech.body:
Dear [Name],

I'm writing about a dual-function shunt concept: CSF drainage + enzymatic Aβ/tau clearance with pulsation-synchronized contact time optimization.

The engineering is frozen (flow range, contact-time equation, drainage floor, pulsation sync mechanism). The biology is not — and we're transparent about that.

We've defined the smallest wet-lab program (8 months, $100-200K) that would answer three questions:
  Phase 1: Which enzyme actually works in CSF? (30-day stability test, 3 candidates)
  Phase 2: Can it remain active when immobilized? (2 immobilization strategies)
  Phase 3: Does pulsation-synchronized flow materially improve clearance? (1.3x target)

Each phase has a go/no-go gate. If Phase 1 fails, we stop. No documentation around a failed enzyme.

The full program is here:
  repo: github.com/prateekm1007/discovery-evidence-fabric
  file: TTP_PACKAGES/P-04_FREEZE/WET_LAB_PROGRAM_SMALLEST.json

If your team has enzyme engineering capability and would be interested in executing or co-executing this program, I'd welcome a conversation. The pulsation-synchronized contact-time lock is the differentiator — if Phase 3 confirms 1.3x improvement, the IP position is defensible.

Best regards,
[Your name]

template_P09_research_funding.target: Chief Scientific Officer or Head of Research at neuro-monitoring company (Raumedic, Codman/Integra), or venture partner at life science VC
template_P09_research_funding.subject: P-09: Chemical molecular ICP signaling — architecture concept + molecule-selection research program
template_P09_research_funding.body:
Dear [Name],

I'm writing about a high-risk, high-differentiation concept: converting ICP into a chemical molecular signal in CSF, detectable by a wearable biosensor — eliminating all electronics, batteries, and RF from the intracranial implant.

The architecture is novel. The molecule is unspecified. I'm not pretending otherwise.

We've defined a 14-month, $200-500K molecule-selection research program with 6 steps:
  1. Candidate molecular mechanisms (5 classes identified)
  2. Feasibility screen (computational chemistry)
  3. Transport model (in silico CSF flow simulation)
  4. Detectability assessment (sensor technology)
  5. Safety constraints (toxicology review)
  6. Shortlist + experimental plan

Each step has a go/no-go gate. Probability of finding a viable molecule: 20-40%. If no molecule is found, the architecture dies — but the negative result is itself valuable.

The full program is here:
  repo: github.com/prateekm1007/discovery-evidence-fabric
  file: TTP_PACKAGES/P-09_ARCHITECTURE_CONCEPT/MOLECULE_SELECTION_RESEARCH_PROGRAM.json

This is a research investment, not a product acquisition. If your organization funds early-stage research with high differentiation potential, I'd welcome a conversation about co-funding or advising on the program.

Best regards,
[Your name]

template_P01_academic_lab.target: PI at academic neurosurgery / bioengineering lab (MIT, Stanford, UCSF, Johns Hopkins, Cleveland Clinic)
template_P01_academic_lab.subject: External validation opportunity: P-01 shunt occlusion-isolation controller simulator + bench protocol
template_P01_academic_lab.body:
Dear Professor [Name],

I'm writing to offer an external validation opportunity for a CSF shunt occlusion-isolation controller.

We've built a Python simulator that falsified our own original claim (strict dual-invariant doesn't hold) but showed that predictive isolation extends time to failure by 7-9x vs conventional single-path shunts. The A/B/C comparison is documented and reproducible.

We've prepared a complete external validation handoff folder:
  - Frozen simulator code (SHA-256 verified)
  - Frozen test protocol (6 scenarios × 5 seeds = 30 bench runs)
  - Pre-registered expected metrics (so you can confirm or refute our prediction)
  - Blinding protocol (to prevent confirmation bias)
  - Result submission JSON schema (so results are comparable across labs)
  - 10 reproducibility checks (to verify your setup matches ours)

The bench prototype costs ~$3-5K and takes 3-6 months to build. The protocol is 720 bench-hours (30 days at 24/7).

All materials are here:
  repo: github.com/prateekm1007/discovery-evidence-fabric
  folder: TTP_PACKAGES/P-01_PROTOTYPE/EXTERNAL_VALIDATION_HANDOFF/

If your lab would be interested in running this validation (independently, without consulting us during analysis), I'd be glad to discuss. Your lab would be acknowledged in the provenance ledger, and the results — whether they confirm or refute our predictions — would be published alongside our original claims.

Best regards,
[Your name]

template_portfolio_VC.target: Life science venture partner (Flagship Pioneering, ARCH Venture, Versant Ventures, GV Life Sciences)
template_portfolio_VC.subject: CereVascular eShunt discovery portfolio — 15 packages, 3 flagships, AI-driven self-correcting discovery loop
template_portfolio_VC.body:
Dear [Name],

I'm writing about a portfolio of 15 cerebrovascular medical device technology packages, built by an AI-driven discovery engine that includes a constitutional epistemic framework (35 articles governing how the system can make claims and correct itself).

Three flagship packages are at different maturity levels:
  P-01: PROTOTYPE_READY. Python simulator falsified the original claim, A/B/C comparison shows 7-9x improvement. Buyer-ready for technical evaluation.
  P-04: Engineering frozen, biology program defined (8-month wet-lab program, $100-200K, with go/no-go gates).
  P-09: Architecture concept for zero-electronics chemical ICP signaling. 14-month molecule-selection research program defined ($200-500K, 20-40% probability of viable molecule).

What's unusual about this portfolio:
1. The discovery engine has a constitution that forces honest labeling (Articles XXV-XXXV). Every claim has a status: VERIFIED, EXTERNAL_SOURCE, MODELLED, HYPOTHESIS, BUYER_UNVERIFIED, MISSING.
2. The system caught its own overclaim in R277 (initial 'survival 5/5' was actually 0/5) and self-corrected before any buyer saw it.
3. Pricing is explicit: $50K vs $500K changes rights (exclusivity, field, territory), NOT evidence quality.

The full portfolio is open-source:
  repo: github.com/prateekm1007/discovery-evidence-fabric

I'm not seeking an acquisition of the portfolio. I'm seeking either:
  - A strategic investment to fund the P-04 wet-lab program ($100-200K) and P-09 molecule program ($200-500K)
  - A partnership to connect us with buyer engineering teams for P-01 technical evaluation

If either is interesting, I'd welcome a conversation.

Best regards,
[Your name]
